result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is from a vision clinic (vision rehabilitation office). It was sent to your doctor. It is about your low vision check.

- You have a history of macular degeneration.
- You say you had PDT (photodynamic therapy) in the last year. The letter does not say which eye. It does not say when.
- You use a small handheld magnifier. It gives you only limited help.
- The clinic found a mild change in your distance correction (glasses for seeing far).
- With the distance correction, you could see 20/70 in the right eye. You could see 20/200 in the left eye.
- With +4 reading glasses, you could read 0.5M print quite nicely.
- The doctor thinks you are an excellent candidate for low vision help.

## What you need to do
1. The clinic has loaned you a pair of +4 reading glasses.
2. The clinic has started fine-detailed reading therapy with you.
3. Come back to the clinic in two weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- Return visit to the vision rehabilitation office: in two weeks. At this visit, the clinic will decide which near reading glasses to prescribe for you.
- The letter does not list any medicines.
- The date of your visit is not known. The letter shows only a placeholder.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What does macular degeneration mean for me?
- How will the loaned +4 reading glasses help me?
- What will happen at my visit in two weeks?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
